text: Using a modified telomeric repeat amplification protocol (TRAP), telomerase activity was detected in crickets, cockroaches, and two Lepidopteran insects, though insect telomeres generally consist of pentanucleotide (TTAGG)n repeats—absent in Diptera and some other species, whose telomeres may be maintained without telomerase. Cricket and cockroach telomerase required dATP, dGTP, and dTTP but not dCTP as substrate; sequence analyses confirmed that (TTAGG)n repeats are synthesized by telomerase. Cockroach telomerase occurred in both somatic cells (fat body, muscle, neural tissues) and germ line (testis), indicating expression is not tissue-specific in adults. High activity appeared in crickets and cockroaches, but none was detected in Bombyx mori tissues or cell cultures, nor in two Drosophila and one Sarcophaga cell line—supporting the theory that Dipteran insects maintain telomeres without telomerase.
